strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas regression (pandas-dev/pandas#57314, buggy commit ada009a40356) where converting near-minimum timestamps to datetime64[ns] raises OverflowError due to intermediate microseconds->nanoseconds scaling overflow; fixed revision adds a special-case in `npy_datetimestruct_to_datetime` to avoid false overflow for a narrow near-boundary window. The reproducer is the newly added test `test_to_datetime_barely_inside_bounds` in `pandas/tests/tslibs/test_array_to_datetime.py`.

pinned_because: No version constraints were provided in the evidence for numpy/cython/pyarrow; only cython is required for building from source per README text. To ensure the bug transitions, use the project’s own test runner with the installed pandas build on each target commit. If your build uses an editable source tree, the test command will exercise the compiled tslib/native code where the overflow check lives.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (ada009a40356), running the test raises an OverflowError (test fails at `tslib.array_to_datetime(...)`). On the fixed revision (the PR that resolves #57150 / #57314), the same call returns a numpy datetime64[ns] array equal to the input timestamps (test passes).
strategy.numerical_probe: The failing path is near-minimum datetime conversion when the base unit is nanoseconds (NPY_FR_ns) and microseconds are in the narrow window where `scaleMicrosecondsToNanoseconds(microseconds, &nanoseconds)` overflows, even though the final nanoseconds-adjusted result would be within int64_t bounds. Use the timestamps: "1677-09-21T00:12:43.145224193" and "1677-09-21T00:12:43.145224999" (and control "1677-09-21T00:12:43.145225000").

input_output_examples.input: 1677-09-21T00:12:43.145224193 (object array element passed to tslib.array_to_datetime; base == NPY_FR_ns)
1677-09-21T00:12:43.145224999 (object array element passed to tslib.array_to_datetime; base == NPY_FR_ns)

input_output_examples.buggy_output: No `OverflowError` (test should pass even on buggy revision)

risks: Platform/toolchain risk: this is native code overflow-check behavior in pandas’ datetime conversion; while the test should be stable across common platforms, failures could be architecture/toolchain-specific if int64 overflow checks behave differently under certain build configurations or compilers.

Dependency-version risk (unbounded in evidence): the provided evidence does not pin numpy/cpython versions; although the bug is within pandas’ own logic (`npy_datetimestruct_to_datetime`) and should transition with just the pandas commit change, confirm on your CI matrix (at least one representative Linux x86_64 setup).
Optional dependency risk: pyarrow is mentioned only as an optional dependency version (14.0.2) with no documented install procedure; do not rely on it for reproduction.
Threading risk: none indicated in the evidence; run tests normally (single-process pytest) to reduce variance.

oracle.reference_source: The test compares output array elements exactly to numpy datetime64[ns] constructed from the same ISO-8601 strings via `np.array([timestamp], dtype="M8[ns]")`.
oracle.why: The reproducing test asserts exact equality of the returned numpy array; it does not use numeric tolerance checks, and success is determined by the transition from exception to equality.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: `test_to_datetime_barely_inside_bounds` fails for the first two parameter values because `tslib.array_to_datetime(np.array([timestamp], dtype=object))` raises `OverflowError` during intermediate `scaleMicrosecondsToNanoseconds` scaling when base is nanoseconds (NPY_FR_ns). The control timestamp is expected to continue working.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying the fix from PR #57314 / issue #57150, the special-case prevents the intermediate overflow for near-minimum values; `tslib.array_to_datetime(...)` completes and returns a numpy array exactly equal to the expected `datetime64[ns]` value for each timestamp parameter.
